title: Spray-pyrolyzed Co-doped CeO 2  thin films for composition-tunable third-order nonlinear optics and optical limiting
content: Cobalt-doped cerium oxide (Co–CeO2) thin films (0, 10, 20, and 30% Co) were fabricated on glass substrates via air-blast spray pyrolysis and annealed at 350 °C to examine composition-dependent linear and third-order nonlinear optical (NLO) responses. X-ray diffraction and whole-pattern refinement were consistent with retention of the cubic fluorite CeO2 lattice across all compositions with progressive peak broadening indicating increased structural disorder at higher Co loadings. Scanning electron microscopy showed a morphological transition from a dense nanogranular surface to fine-grained, microcracked domain networks with energy-dispersive X-ray (EDX) mapping confirming homogeneous Ce, O, and Co distribution. X-ray photoelectron spectra indicated changes in near-surface oxygen and cation chemical environments. Co incorporation red-shifted the optical absorption edge, reducing the direct and indirect bandgaps from 3.32 and 2.87 eV (direct) to 2.79 and 2.43 eV (indirect), correspondingly, while the Urbach energy expanded from 1.24 to 1.74 eV, confirming enhanced sub-bandgap tail states. Open-aperture (OA) Z-scan measurements (at 532 nm) revealed reverse saturable absorption (RSA) with the nonlinear absorption coefficient increasing from 6.6 × 10−2 to 16.2 × 10−2 cm W−1 from undoped to 30% Co films. Closed-aperture (CA) measurements demonstrated positive nonlinear refraction, where the 20% Co film achieved the maximum nonlinear refractive response and total third-order susceptibility (χ(3)). Conversely, the 30% Co film yielded the highest absorptive nonlinearity and the lowest optical limiting threshold (1.80 kJ cm−2). These results establish composition-selective functionality in spray-pyrolyzed Co–CeO2 thin films: 20% Co optimizes phase modulation and overall, third-order NLO response, whereas 30% Co is ideal for absorption-driven optical limiting.
